lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about his exact status at the moment. He's 16, so he's at that age where things are a bit up in the air. I know he's not working full-time or anything like that, but I'm not certain about whether he's in education or what his plans are right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's quite a common situation at that age. Let me ask a few more questions to help clarify:

**Is Alex currently attending school, college, or sixth form at all, even if you're not sure about his long-term plans?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not attending school or college at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Has Alex registered with a careers service (like the National Careers Service) or is he considering joining the armed services?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if he's registered with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask about his work situation to get a clearer picture:

**You mentioned he's not working full-time - is Alex doing any paid work at all? If so, do you know roughly how many hours per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing any paid work at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. A couple more questions:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

## Summary

Based on the information you've provided, **I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**What we know:**
- Alex is 16 and lives with you in the UK
- He's not currently in education or training
- He's not working or claiming benefits

**The issue:**
Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training. Since Alex isn't currently in education, your eligibility would depend on:

1. **Whether Alex was previously in education** and when he left
2. **Whether he has registered with a careers service** (like the National Careers Service) - if he left education recently and registered with such a service, you could get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks

**What you should do:**
I'd recommend finding out:
- When Alex left education (if he did)
- Whether he has registered with any careers service or is considering the armed services

Once you have this information, you could contact the Child Benefit Office directly, or if you'd like, you can come back with those details and I can give you a clearer answer about your eligibility.
